original_question: Is every 6-dimensional polytope 3-linked, in the sense that for every choice of three pairs of distinct vertices there exist three pairwise disjoint paths in its graph, each connecting one chosen pair?
target_in_paper: The supplied arXiv ID 1806.01163 does not match the draft topic; the draft instead matches Section 4, Problem 1 of Axel Werner and Ronald F. Wotzlaw, On linkages in polytope graphs: "Determine k(6): Either show that all 6-polytopes are 3-linked, or give an example of a 6-polytope P with k(P) = 2."
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core open problem well: it is about 6-dimensional polytopes, asks whether they are 3-linked, and correctly spells out the path-linkage condition in the graph of the polytope.
missing_details: The provided paper identifier arXiv:1806.01163 is unrelated to polytope linkedness; the matching source is Werner–Wotzlaw's On linkages in polytope graphs.
The official formulation is framed as determining the minimal linkedness k(6), not just as a yes/no universal statement.
It should explicitly require that the six terminals are six distinct vertices overall, not merely that each of the three pairs consists of distinct vertices.
It should explicitly refer to the graph G(P) of a 6-dimensional convex polytope P.
In the paper's terminology, the paths are vertex-disjoint; 'pairwise disjoint' should be made precise as vertex-disjoint.
The paper gives the equivalent counterexample formulation: either prove every 6-polytope is 3-linked or exhibit a 6-polytope P with k(P) = 2.

Nearby context in the paper explains why this is the right sharp question: Theorem 2.2 gives k(6) >= 2, Corollary 3.7 gives k(6) <= 3, and the Section 4 discussion records evidence from Theorem 3.11 plus enumeration that several small-vertex cases already satisfy 3-linkedness.
refined_question: Determine the minimal linkedness k(6) of 6-dimensional convex polytopes, where k(6) := min{k(P) : P is a 6-polytope} and k(P) is the largest integer k such that for every choice of 2k distinct vertices s1, ..., sk, t1, ..., tk in the graph G(P), there exist k pairwise vertex-disjoint paths in G(P) joining si to ti for i = 1, ..., k. Is k(6) = 3?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: either show that every 6-dimensional convex polytope is 3-linked, or construct a 6-polytope P with k(P) = 2.
justification: The draft is not faithful to the supplied arXiv ID, because arXiv:1806.01163 is VADU 2018 Open Problem Session, an optimization paper rather than a polytope-linkedness paper. The draft instead matches Werner–Wotzlaw's linkedness paper. There, Section 1 defines k-linked graphs, k(P), and k(d); Section 2.1 proves the general lower bound k(d) >= floor((d + 2)/3), giving k(6) >= 2; Corollary 3.7 gives k(d) <= floor((2d + 3)/5), hence k(6) <= 3; and Section 4 then states that k(6) is the first open value and formulates Problem 1 exactly as determining whether k(6) = 3 or whether some 6-polytope has k(P) = 2. The nearby Section 4 discussion, referring back to Theorem 3.11, records evidence k(6,0) = k(6,1) = k(6,2) = 3 and an enumerative verification that k(6,3) = 3, which is useful context but not part of the problem statement itself.
